source_ref: Lee Y, Kim SK, Eom M-R (2020) 'Usability of mental illness simulation involving scenarios with patients with schizophrenia via immersive virtual reality: A mixed methods study', PLOS ONE 15(9):e0238437, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0238437 (CC BY 4.0). ITEM TEXT and VERIFICATION: article JATS XML Table 2 'Responses to usability scale statement (n = 60)' (No/Item/Range/Mean/SD), structured text in the XML, not OCR (article.xml sha256 7e19c1857ce967eb3ac756d0df5bd87ce7bb793fb9487ef468960f54f950fbff). DEPOSIT: S1 Data .sav (PLOS s001, sha256 17143fe5a04b6380b30c95bc16033c36932c2170c10a733b5195a4bb69568aab); S2 xlsx open-ended responses (s002, sha256 bf5ab2c7f9298e18b5490c980b751d0e4986378cf145fd6c7e7c1ef61a8e0aa8); S3 device manual PDF; S4/S5 response-to-reviewers docx. Processing script data/lee_2020_vr_usability.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/lee_2020_vr_usability/.
note: PASS with disclosures (batch_319). 187 rows = 17 items x resp 0-10; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets. CODE DERIVATION: pattern 1 -- data/lee_2020_vr_usability.py melts the .sav's Usability* columns by name, no rename. The .sav's variable labels are only 'ease of use 1'..'ease of use 11' (Usability1-11) and 'usefulness1'..'usefulness6' (Usability12-17), no wording and no value labels on the items, so no data_labels claim; the code-to-text tie is Table 2's 'No' column 1..17, which numbers the items in the same two domain blocks (Ease of use 1-11, Usefulness 12-17) -> paper_explicit. STEP 3b: live shape (17 items, 0-10, n=60 each) matches the paper's 17-item quantitative usability questionnaire ('responses on a scale ranging from 0 to 10 ... ease of use (11 items) and usefulness (6 items)'); the 7-item open-ended questionnaire is not in this table. No mismatch. STEP 5b VERIFIED (verify_lee_2020_vr_usability.R, VERDICT: PASS): live per-item mean and SD reproduce Table 2 for every item at 2dp (e.g. U1 8.383/1.263 vs 8.38/1.26; U2 9.250/1.002 vs 9.25/1.00; U14 8.583/1.369 vs 8.58/1.37; U15 8.633/1.089 vs 8.63/1.09; U17 8.900/1.423 vs 8.90/1.42); the 17 published means are all distinct and the near pairs (8.58/8.60, 8.63/8.65) are separated by SD (1.37/1.30, 1.09/1.57); the reverse-worded item 7 ('It was difficult to operate the devices') is the only item with mean < 5. SOURCE/DATA DISCREPANCIES (numbers so they can be re-checked): (a) Usability7: Table 2 prints 2.60 / 2.61 / range 0-8; live is 2.767 / 2.752 / 0-10. The only 10 is participant M12 (14 of 17 items at 10). Reading that one value as 0 reproduces Table 2 exactly (2.6000 / 2.6051 / 0-8, n=60); dropping it does not (2.644, n=59). So the paper analysed M12's item 7 as 0 while the deposit, and IRW, hold 10 -- a single-cell response-data discrepancy, not an item-text issue; IRW data left as deposited. (b) Usability5: Table 2 prints SD 1.5; data give 1.954 (mean 7.75 matches) -- misprint in the paper. (c) Usability9: Table 2 prints range 5-10; data give 2-10 (mean 6.83, SD 1.98 match) -- misprint in the paper. LANGUAGE: administered in Korean (60 nursing students, Mokpo National University, Korea; the S2 xlsx shows the open-ended questionnaire was administered in Korean, with the authors' English gloss in row 1). The Korean wording of the 17 quantitative items is published nowhere in the record: the article XML items are English, the .sav labels are English domain tags, S2 holds only the 7 open-ended questions and answers, S3 is an English device manual and S4/S5 are reviewer responses (0 Hangul). So fallback: English from Table 2 in base fields, _translated columns omitted, language=Korean, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. TRANSCRIPTION: item text verbatim from Table 2, character for character. instructions blank (none published). option_text blank for all rows: the paper says only 'a scale ranging from 0 to 10' and that higher = more favourable (except item 7); no anchor labels printed, and no scale point padded with its number. All 11 levels emitted for every item. Instrument name is descriptive (the paper gives the questionnaire no title); section_id single trivial -- the Ease of use / Usefulness domains are table headings, not administered prompts. RIGHTS: the questionnaire is the authors' own ('developed based on the existing literature and previously-developed usability tests'), printed in a CC BY 4.0 article; no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause exists or was located. Silence is permission; not blocked; no register row written.
public_note: Respondents were Korean nursing students and the questionnaire was administered in Korean, but the Korean wording of these 17 items is not published, so IRW ships the English the paper prints in its Table 2, with language recorded as Korean; separately, one Usability7 response (participant M12) is 10 in the deposited data while the paper's Table 2 statistics for that item (mean 2.60, SD 2.61, range 0-8) are reproduced only if that response is 0.

Words: item_text is those deposit column labels verbatim (terse labels, not the on-screen question); the administered wording was never published -- Ozono et al. 2021 BRM (PMC7880926, CC BY) and the deposit's 'description of data.pdf' only paraphrase: 'participants reported how much they were interested in the magic tricks in general (1 being not at all and 10 being very much) and whether they perform magic tricks themselves (1 being not at all, 2 being a little bit and 3 being frequently)'. Instructions left blank (none published). Option axis carries inference: the paper/description state 1..10 and 1..3, but the participant file (and so the live table) stores 0..9 (n=451) and 0..2 (n=450; one blank cell dropped by the script); the deposit's own 'rating data.csv' stores its 10-point ratings as 1..10, so the -1 shift is specific to the participant file. Anchors shipped as stored = described - 1: interest 0='not at all', 9='very much', 1..8 blank (unlabelled points); performing 0='not at all', 1='a little bit', 2='frequently'. Direction checked (verify_magiccats_ozono_2020.R): general interest correlates Spearman +0.375 with the same 451 respondents' mean per-trick 'Interest in the trick' (1..10, 1=not at all); performing 379/65/6 at 0/1/2 (84.2% at 0 in an MTurk sample) and mean general interest rises 5.92/7.18/7.67 across performing levels. Rights: two ad hoc study questions; paper CC BY 4.0; OSF node carries no licence; the deposit's 'Applicaition form for MagicCATs.pdf' restricts the VIDEO files only ('The MagicCATs videos can be used only for research purpose'; 'will not share the video files') -- no clause on the rating questions (silence). The wording is in any case already the response table's item codes.
